html:
Sol Plaatje was a South African journalist, writer and translator, a founder of the African National Congress (ANC), and author of the first novel in English by a black South African.

Largely self-taught, he spoke many languages and worked as a court interpreter at Mafeking. During the siege of Mafeking in the Second Boer War he kept a diary, published long after his death. He then edited newspapers in Setswana and English.

In 1912 he became the first general secretary of the South African Native National Congress, later the ANC. The next year the Natives Land Act barred black South Africans from owning land in most of the country. Plaatje travelled to Britain to protest and wrote Native Life in South Africa (1916), which opens: "Awaking on Friday morning, June 20, 1913, the South African native found himself, not actually a slave, but a pariah in the land of his birth."

His novel Mhudi, set in the wars of the 1830s, appeared in 1930. He also translated Shakespeare into Setswana. The municipality that includes Kimberley now bears his name.
sum: Sol Plaatje was a South African journalist, writer and translator, a founder of the African National Congress (ANC), and author of the first novel in English by a black South African.
